narrative: New England fell to JAX 6-35. The offense posted -0.25 EPA/play (37% success rate) while the defense allowed 0.23 EPA/play. Turnover margin was -2.

good: Rhamondre Stevenson was the bright spot, posting 7% win probability added—the only player on either side generating meaningful positive momentum.
Marcus Jones recorded his first interception of the season, a rare defensive bright spot in an otherwise dismal day.
bad: The red zone offense was an absolute disaster: 0 touchdowns on 4 trips, while Jacksonville scored on all 5 of theirs—a 5 TD performance that basically decided the game.
Drake Maye's three turnovers (two interceptions and a lost fumble) and the offense's -0.25 EPA per play told the whole story: this unit is struggling mightily right now.
Third down conversion rate of 4 for 12 (33%) falls well short of the league average, and that kind of offensive futility on manageable downs compounds every other problem.
ugly: The defensive unit allowed 8 of 12 third downs (67%)—nearly double the league norm—and couldn't stop Jacksonville's offense when it mattered, surrendering five touchdown drives.

playerOfTheGame.reason: Led the team with +7% win probability added.

fanTake: Well, that was genuinely difficult to watch. The Patriots traveled to Jacksonville and got thoroughly dismantled, 35-6, in a performance that left Drake Maye calling his own offense "unacceptable"—and frankly, it's hard to argue with him after three turnovers and a unit that managed just two field goals all afternoon. Jacksonville's defense made life miserable, while the Jaguars' offense (led by Lawrence's three touchdown passes) operated like they were playing a different sport entirely. The gap between what this team needs to be and what it showed up as on Sunday was genuinely alarming.
